title: Speculative Decode: Kernel Routing, KV Warmup & Telemetry Proposal
content:
Summary:
This doc proposes a combined design for (1) kernel-aware routing used by speculative decoding, (2) a lightweight KV-cache warmup policy for model-variant transitions, and (3) a compact telemetry & rollback signal set to enable safe canaries. Goal: improve speculative decode throughput while bounding tail latency and giving ops deterministic rollback criteria when model variants or kernel selections regress.

Motivation / Context:
- We run speculative decoding using fast approximate variants (quantized, shorter contexts) as the speculative path and high-fidelity variants as the confirm path.
- Empirically we've seen cases where kernel mismatch or cold KV-cache makes the speculative step slower than expected (misspeculative cost).
- Current rollouts rely on throughput and p50/p99 latency dashboards but lack an actionable numeric regression signal to auto-fallback.

High-level design:
1) Kernel-aware routing table: requests annotated with expected sequence-length distribution + model-variant tags. Routing picks the kernel-plus-queue (fast-quantized, fp16, int8-x) that historically yields best SLO for that tuple.
2) Speculative-decoding admission: lightweight classifier uses prefix-length, active KV-hit-rate estimate, and model-variant stability score to decide whether to speculative-decode for a given request.
3) KV-cache warmup policy: on model-variant switch (canary -> prod), we perform progressive warmup by forwarding a controlled fraction of requests through the confirm variant to populate KV entries (see warmup algorithm below).
4) Telemetry & rollback signals: define Speculative Efficiency Ratio (SER), Misspeculative Cost (MC), and Corrective Rollback Score (CRS) as compact signals for automated gating.

Kernel routing heuristics (detailed):
- Each model-variant V is mapped to one or more kernel profiles K. Profile metadata: preferred sequence range, memory footprint, batching sweet spot, observed per-token latency.
- Routing decision inputs: request.expected_seq_len_bucket, current_batch_size_estimate, kv_cache_estimated_hit_rate, tenant_priority
- Scoring: score(K|V,req) = w1 * latency_est(K,V,seq) + w2 * tail_risk(K,V) + w3 * cost_per_token(K,V)
- We default to favor kernels with slightly higher per-token cost if tail risk is reduced (operationally prefer lower p99).

Admission classifier for speculative decoding:
- Features: prefix_length_bucket, kv_hit_rate_est, recent_miss_rate_per_variant, rolling_latency_delta, sequence_variability_flag
- Output: probability p_spec that speculative decode will be net-positive. Thresholds tunable by tier: p_spec_threshold = 0.6 for free tier, 0.4 for enterprise (since enterprise tolerates more cost to reduce latency).
- Rationale: avoid speculative decoding when cold KV-cache would almost certainly force confirm decode anyway.

KV-cache warmup algorithm (progressive):
1) Phase 0: canary baseline (0% warmup) — measure cold-hit penalty and baseline correctness.
2) Phase 1: warmup-fraction F=5% — for a random 5% of eligible requests, route confirm path but retain speculative accounting. This populates KV for common prefixes.
3) Phase 2: F=25% — expand to more prefixes and observe SER, MC.
4) Phase 3: Full rollout (F=100%) once metrics stable and CRS < threshold.
Warmup selection: prefer high-frequency prefixes first (top 5% prefixes by occurrence), then moving window. This avoids warming long-tail cold prefixes that are expensive.

Telemetry & metric definitions:
- Speculative Efficiency Ratio (SER) = (tokens_served_speculatively_that_avoided_confirm) / (tokens_processed_speculative + confirm_extra_tokens_due_to_misspeculation)
  - Intuition: fraction of token effort that was useful. Target >0.6 for rollout.
- Misspeculative Cost (MC) = average additional tokens and latency incurred when speculative was used but confirm still executed. Units: tokens + ms normalized to cost units.
- Corrective Rollback Score (CRS) = weighted combination of p99 latency uplift, SER drop, error-rate delta and token-cost delta. CRS > 1.0 signals rollback candidate. (We will normalize so current baseline CRS=0.0).
- Additional signals: kernel-switch-flip-rate (how often routing flips kernel for same model in steady state), kv_warmth_fraction, prefix-hit-entropy.

Rollback and automated failsafes:
- Hard triggers (immediate rollback): p99_latency increase > 30% for 10m AND error-rate delta > 0.5x for 5m.
- Soft triggers (investigate & pause): CRS > 0.8 for 30m or SER drops < 0.4 for 1h.
- Automated rollback procedure: API that flips routing table to last-known-good kernel profile and reduces speculative admission to 0% for the affected variant, then executes a partial warmup to rebaseline.
- Safety net: when rollback happens, mark the model-variant as quarantined and create a ticket with dump of recent traces and top-100 prefixes causing misses.

Testing & validation plan:
- Microbench harness: synthetic sequences with controlled KV-hit distributions and sequence-length histograms to measure kernel mapping performance.
- Replay: run 7-day traffic replay to simulate warmup progression and compute SER, MC.
- Canary runs: choose 1 high-throughput tenant + 2 medium tenants for phased rollout. Observe 48h sliding metrics before expanding.
- Chaos test: randomly drop KV-cache for 1% of requests to measure system reaction and resilience of admission classifier.

Operational checklist for onboarding a new model variant:
- Kernel compatibility tests passed (unit + perf) — record results in PR.
- Synthetic SER > 0.65 for default kernel mapping.
- Canary run for 48h with CRS < 0.5.
- KV warmup plan scheduled (Phase 1 and Phase 2 windows).
- Telemetry hooks: ensure SER, MC, CRS, kernel-switch metrics emitted.
- Rollback playbook attached to release notes.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should the admission classifier be for low-volume tenants? Tighter thresholds reduce cost but may hurt latency experienced by end-users.
- Should kernel routing be tenant-aware (preferred) or purely model-variant aware? Tenant-specific routing can improve p99 at the cost of bigger routing tables.
- Cold-start cost: we approximate cost by prefix frequency; long-tail prefixes still expensive — consider background synthetic warmup to cover rare prefixes for important customers.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [Samir] prototype admission classifier in go-runner and evaluate on replay (ETA 2026-03-03).
- [Lena] add telemetry: SER, MC, CRS to per-model dashboards and traces (ETA 2026-03-07).
- [Diego] implement routing table schema changes to include kernel metadata (ETA 2026-03-12).
- [Priya] write rollback automation script and test in staging (ETA 2026-03-14).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: the team needs a compact operational signal to avoid slow, noisy rollouts. Please focus review on the telemetry definitions (SER/CRS) and the warmup fractions — they are tunable knobs.
- If you have historical incidents where speculative decoding caused regressions, paste the incident ID in comments so we can replay similar traffic during validation.
